summary: SCT fails 3 of 4 pre-registered decision criteria on Taboo/Direct (primary benchmark) and performs worse than the logit lens baseline on User Gender/Direct (secondary). The suppression-contrast method does not yield meaningful improvements over standard logit lens.
analysis: On Taboo/Direct, the best SCT variant (filtered logit lens with cross-model generic token filter) achieved TR@5=5.33% and auditor accuracy=3.07%, compared to the constrained logit lens baseline of TR@5=4.33% and auditor=4.17%. The TR@5 improvement (+23.1% relative, +1.0pp absolute) falls short of both pre-registered thresholds (>=25% relative, >=1.5pp absolute). Critically, the auditor accuracy actually decreased from 4.17% to 3.07%, meaning SCT fails criterion 4. The suppression premise (criterion 1) is also unsupported: secret tokens appear at mid-layer control positions in only ~9.3% of examples vs the required 30%. Only the mechanism check (criterion 3) passed: DoLa-direction (reversed contrast) performs drastically worse than logit lens (0.20% vs 4.33% TR@5), confirming the direction of suppression is informative. On User Gender/Direct, SCT performs worse than logit lens on both metrics (auditor: 51.25% vs 56.70%, TR@5: 1.20% vs 6.95%). Compared to published baselines, SCT's auditor accuracy (3.07% on Taboo) is below LL Tokens (4.13%), and far below black-box methods like User Persona (7.17%). The best SCT variant turned out to be filtered logit lens -- not actually using the suppression contrast signal -- confirming the core SCT mechanism provides no additional value.
reason: The verdict is 'bad' because: (1) the suppression premise is unsupported (only ~9.3% of examples show mid-layer secret token presence vs 30% threshold), (2) token-recovery improvement fails both thresholds (+23.1% relative < 25%, +1.0pp < 1.5pp), (3) auditor accuracy is worse for SCT (3.07%) than baseline logit lens (4.17%), (4) the method does not generalize to User Gender (worse than LL on all metrics), and (5) the best-performing variant after optimization is actually filtered logit lens, not the proposed suppression-contrast scoring -- meaning the core SCT idea (mid-minus-final layer contrast) adds no value. The approach needs to be fundamentally reconsidered.
